images.title: Four rows of a 9 slit mat
images.purpose: Show the example of the concept: each row is the row above moved one slit to the right, and the fourth row is the same as the first, so the rows repeat after 3 rows.
images.composition: A four row weave on nine slits with the row names on the left, Row 1 and Row 4 outlined in the same colour with an arrow joining them, and the finding written below.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. TOP LEFT: the title A mat with 9 slits in dark #1F2937 sans-serif bold (40 px), left edge at x 60, about y 55. THE GRID: exactly 4 rows by 9 columns of crossings, 36 cells in all, every cell an 80 by 80 px rounded square (corner radius 8 px) with a thin dark #2B2B2B outline (3 px) and 6 px between cells. The 9 columns start at x 330 and end at x 1098 (cell c, counted from 1 at the left, starts at x 330 + 86 times (c minus 1)); the 4 rows have their tops at y 120, 206, 292 and 378 (the bottom of the grid is y 458). A cell is TEAL #0072B2 where the strip goes over and CREAM #F5E6C8 where it goes under. Rows from the top, cells from the left: row 1: over, under, under, over, under, under, over, under, under (teal in cells 1, 4 and 7); row 2: under, over, under, under, over, under, under, over, under (teal in cells 2, 5 and 8); row 3: under, under, over, under, under, over, under, under, over (teal in cells 3, 6 and 9); row 4: over, under, under, over, under, under, over, under, under (teal in cells 1, 4 and 7). So every row has 3 teal and 6 cream cells (12 teal, 24 cream in all), each row is the row above moved one slit to the right, and row 4 is exactly the same as row 1. ROW NAMES: the texts Row 1, Row 2, Row 3 and Row 4, each centred at x 215 and at the middle height of its row (y 168, 254, 340 and 426), 40 px, dark. HIGHLIGHT: two reddish purple #CC79A7 rounded outline rectangles (6 px, no fill), one round row 1 (x 322 to 1106, y 112 to 208) and one round row 4 (x 322 to 1106, y 370 to 466). A thin reddish purple curved arrow (5 px) on the right of the grid starts at the right edge of the row 4 outline (x 1106, y 418), bends out to x 1188, and ends with its arrowhead on the right edge of the row 1 outline (x 1106, y 160). TEXT BELOW THE GRID: at y 520 centred at x 714 the text Row 4 is the same as Row 1 in reddish purple #CC79A7 (40 px), and at y 590 centred at x 714 the bold dark text The rows repeat after 3 rows (56 px), the largest text in the frame. LEGEND at y 660 to 716: a teal 56 by 56 px square at x 330 with the text over: the strip lies on top beside it (36 px, dark, left edge x 410), and a cream 56 by 56 px square with a thin dark outline at x 760 with the text under: the strip goes below beside it (36 px, dark, left edge x 840). Nothing else in the frame.

images.takeaway: Move the row one slit along each time and write the rows until one is the same as Row 1: then the pattern repeats.
images.description: Four rows of a 9 slit mat, each moved one slit to the right, where Row 4 is the same as Row 1.
images.context: Concept image for Rows That Repeat. It follows the idea of the weave rows in your maths book (rows written until the pattern starts to repeat) and uses the concept's own mat of 9 slits.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the child to put a finger on the first teal cell of each row and watch it move one place right. The slip to watch: starting every row at the same place in the pattern.

image_decisions.why: The four rows of the 9 slit mat show the rows coming round to Row 1 again after 3 rows.
